name: David Heinemeier Hansson
category: Software engineer / open-source framework creator (Ruby on Rails)
milestone_by_age_26: Open-sourced Ruby on Rails in 2004 at age 24 after extracting the framework from Basecamp development at 37signals; widely adopted web MVC framework.
early_history_summary: Born October 15, 1979 in Copenhagen. Built gaming review sites in high school with PHP, founded Daily Rush (Danish gaming news community) ~1999–2001, then was hired by Jason Fried to build Basecamp and extracted Rails from that work.
family_context_summary: Born and raised in Copenhagen, Denmark; detailed parental professions not strongly documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: PHP teen projects, Daily Rush, Basecamp extraction, Jason Fried partnership, open-source wave
evidence_summary: DHH built web products as a teen, shipped Daily Rush, then partnered with Jason Fried at 37signals. Extracting and open-sourcing Rails (2004) at 24 made him a defining figure of the mid-2000s web stack. Advantage stack is skill plus complementary partner and structural open-source/SaaS wave rather than inherited capital.
starting_point: Born Copenhagen, Denmark, 1979; learned PHP building gaming sites in high school; later studied at Copenhagen Business School.
current_position: CTO/partner at 37signals (Basecamp/HEY); creator of Ruby on Rails and Omarchy; also endurance racing driver.

trajectory.event: Founded Daily Rush, a Danish online gaming news community, while deep in early web programming.
Hired by Jason Fried to build the project that became Basecamp at 37signals.
Open-sourced Ruby on Rails, extracted from Basecamp's codebase.
Named Google/O'Reilly Hacker of the Year; moved to Chicago after graduating CBS.
Co-authored REWORK with Jason Fried, expanding his product philosophy audience.
Competed seriously in FIA WEC/Le Mans endurance racing while remaining 37signals CTO.

name: Tracy Young
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded PlanGrid in 2011 at about age 26, building a mobile construction blueprint platform later acquired by Autodesk for ~$875M.
early_history_summary: Civil engineering background with early exposure to construction site pain points around paper blueprints. Co-founded PlanGrid with Ralph Gootee, Kenny Stone, and Antoine Hersen to digitize construction drawings for the iPad era.
family_context_summary: Family/financial background not strongly detailed in reviewed sources; engineering-trained entrepreneur.
primary_early_advantage_tags: civil engineering domain, iPad construction wave, cofounder team
evidence_summary: Young translated civil-engineering field pain into PlanGrid at the iPad moment, co-founding with a complementary technical team in 2011 (~age 26). Autodesk's later ~$875M acquisition validated the product. Advantage is domain proximity and team rather than inherited wealth or elite pipeline documentation.
starting_point: Born ~1985; civil-engineering path into construction tech entrepreneurship (detailed childhood not documented in reviewed sources).
current_position: Entrepreneur and investor after PlanGrid's Autodesk acquisition; construction-tech operator turned exit founder.

trajectory.event: Co-founded PlanGrid to replace paper blueprints with mobile construction collaboration.
Scaled PlanGrid across major contractors as mobile construction software adoption grew.
Autodesk acquired PlanGrid for approximately $875 million.

name: Gustaf Alströmer
category: Startup founder / YC partner (Heysan, Airbnb growth)
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Heysan (YC W07) around 2007 at about age 24, entering the Y Combinator ecosystem as a founder before later growth leadership at Airbnb and YC partnership.
early_history_summary: Swedish entrepreneur who co-founded mobile messaging startup Heysan in YC's Winter 2007 batch. Later became Head of Growth at Voxer, then helped start Airbnb's growth team as Product Lead, then returned to YC as a Group/General Partner.
family_context_summary: Swedish background; detailed family wealth/professions not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: YC W07, mobile messaging wave, later Airbnb growth network
evidence_summary: Alströmer's by-26 milestone is founding Heysan in YC W07 (~2007, age ~24). Later career leverage came from Airbnb growth and YC partnership rather than a legendary consumer product of his own. Network compounding after the early YC entry is the dominant later story.
starting_point: Born ~1983 in Sweden; early career through European tech into Y Combinator founder path.
current_position: General Partner / Group Partner at Y Combinator advising hundreds of startups on growth and product.

trajectory.event: Co-founded Heysan in Y Combinator W07 batch.
Joined Airbnb and helped start the company's growth team as Product Lead.
Joined Y Combinator as a partner focused on growth and founder coaching.

name: Immad Akhund
category: Fintech / developer tools founder (Clickpass, Heyzap, Mercury)
milestone_by_age_26: Founded his first startup around 2006 and went through Y Combinator with Clickpass in the mid/late 2000s at about ages 23–24, beginning a multi-startup founder path before Heyzap and Mercury.
early_history_summary: Born in Pakistan, raised in the UK, studied at Cambridge. Founded first company ~2006, then Clickpass (identity/login product) via YC, later co-founded Heyzap (sold ~$45M in 2016) and Mercury (2017).
family_context_summary: Pakistani-born; moved to London as a child; Cambridge-educated. Detailed parental wealth not documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Cambridge, YC, serial founding, immigrant path
evidence_summary: Akhund's material by-26 milestone is early founding (~2006) and YC-backed Clickpass in his early twenties. Later Heyzap exit and Mercury unicorn are post-26. Elite education plus YC network accelerated serial founding more than family capital.
starting_point: Born Pakistan ~1983; moved to London as a child; Cambridge University then Silicon Valley via YC.
current_position: Co-founder and CEO of Mercury (startup banking); active angel investor with hundreds of investments; former YC part-time partner.

trajectory.event: Founded first startup and began multi-year founder path toward YC.
Built Clickpass through the Y Combinator ecosystem as an early identity product.
Co-founded Heyzap, a mobile developer tools company (YC path).
Sold Heyzap for about $45 million.
Co-founded Mercury, digital banking for startups.

name: Deepinder Goyal
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Foodiebay (later Zomato) on July 10, 2008 at age 25 while at Bain, launching India's major restaurant discovery and later food-delivery platform.
early_history_summary: Born January 26, 1983 in Muktsar, Punjab. IIT Delhi graduate who joined Bain & Company; with Pankaj Chaddah built Foodiebay menus/reviews product in 2008, quit Bain in 2009, incorporated 2010 and rebranded to Zomato.
family_context_summary: Born Muktsar, Punjab; IIT path implies selective education. Detailed parental professions not strongly documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: IIT Delhi, Bain, cofounder Chaddah, India internet consumer wave
evidence_summary: Goyal's IIT + Bain credentials and cofounder partnership enabled Foodiebay/Zomato at 25. The product rode India's smartphone/internet consumer wave into a public company (Eternal). Family capital not documented; institutional pipeline and complementary team dominate the early stack.
starting_point: Born Muktsar, Punjab, 1983; IIT Delhi then Bain & Company analyst before founding Foodiebay.
current_position: Founder and longtime CEO of Zomato/Eternal; also founded Temple and LAT Aerospace side efforts.

trajectory.event: Launched Foodiebay (later Zomato) with Pankaj Chaddah while at Bain.
Incorporated the company and rebranded to Zomato; left Bain to go full-time.
Expanded into food delivery, which became the core business.
Took Zomato public in India, creating major wealth and brand visibility.
Parent entity rebranded around Eternal as multi-business consumer internet group.

name: Peyush Bansal
milestone_by_age_26: Incorporated Valyoo Technologies (later Lenskart) in 2008 at age 23 after earlier SearchMyCampus (2007); launched Lenskart online eyewear operations by 2010 at age 25.
early_history_summary: Born April 26, 1985 in New Delhi. Studied engineering, worked at Microsoft, started SearchMyCampus in 2007, then with partners founded Valyoo/Lenskart focusing first on contact lenses then full eyewear retail and manufacturing.
family_context_summary: Born New Delhi to Bal Kishan and Kiran Bansal per secondary bios; middle-class professional path into engineering/Microsoft.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as eyewear-industry family in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Microsoft experience, cofounders, India e-commerce wave, SearchMyCampus warmup
evidence_summary: Bansal founded Valyoo/Lenskart by age 23–25 after a brief Microsoft stint and campus portal experiment. Complementary cofounders and India e-commerce timing matter more than inherited retail networks. Later Shark Tank India fame and IPO path are post-26.
starting_point: Born New Delhi 1985; engineering education; early Microsoft engineer before entrepreneurship.
current_position: Co-founder, Chairman/MD/CEO of Lenskart; Shark Tank India investor-judge; company scaled toward IPO/unicorn status.

trajectory.event: Started SearchMyCampus, a campus services portal experiment.
Incorporated Valyoo Technologies with cofounders (later Lenskart).
Launched Lenskart online eyewear retail operations in India.
Became a Shark Tank India shark, expanding public profile.
Lenskart advanced toward major public-market / liquidity events amid multi-billion valuation.
